quote: And then I think there were before, there was issues with credit. Is your credit score above 670 now?
stewart_read: The rep correctly recalls a past disqualifying issue but doesn't probe what changed, what the customer's current situation is, or set a clear plan to verify before appointment day — he asks the question and moves past the answer without resolution.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be intentionally deferring the credit check to the appointment itself, treating the setter's job as just booking and letting the closer verify credit on-site. However, the rep explicitly gates the appointment on it ('if the credit is good, can we do Monday') without ever closing that loop, undermining this reading.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to either get a firmer commitment ('text me your score tonight so we lock this in') or explicitly tell the customer the appointment proceeds regardless and the closer verifies credit — right now it's left in limbo.

quote: Let me text you so you have my phone number.
stewart_read: The rep offers his personal number as a workaround for confirming the credit/appointment details, the exact anti-pattern the schema flags as a privacy and scale exposure risk on the setter floor.
coaching_implication: Flag for the floor's privacy/security review per schema — this is the detection signal the schema explicitly calls out ('rep verbatim contains... text me at [number]').

quote: I'm I'm gonna be at home Monday, Tuesday, or Wednesday.
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a wide-open, fully cooperative three-day window — an ideal moment to run remaining Verify items (address/homeowner confirm, co-owner, roof, utility, bill) while the customer is engaged. The rep instead jumps straight to scheduling logistics and the credit question, skipping the qualification conversation entirely.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be relying on notes from the prior in-person meeting ('we met with you a while back') to cover Verify items already captured then, which would justify compression per call_shape's note on context-justified compression for repeat touches. But nothing in the transcript confirms those items were captured, and the rep doesn't reference any specifics from the prior meeting to support this.
coaching_implication: When a customer opens a wide cooperative window like this, the rep should use it — even briefly — to reconfirm homeowner status, co-owner, and bill/utility basics rather than jumping straight to credit and time. This is a missed opportunity, not just a skipped script line.

quote: let me text you so you have my phone number. As far as scheduling, though, if the credit is good, can we do Monday morning or afternoon? What would be best?
stewart_read: This stretch (roughly 01:32-01:55) contains lines tagged 'rep' that are clearly customer responses given the diarizer's known failure mode ('I prefer' and 'afternoon' both tagged rep immediately after the rep asks an open question) — the time-negotiation and possibly the credit-check exchange may be customer lines misattributed to the rep track.
alternative_hypothesis: It's possible the transcript is accurate and the rep is talking to himself/rehearsing options aloud, but this is inconsistent with natural call flow and far more likely a diarization artifact per the known SESSION20000555055 pattern.
coaching_implication: Do not coach the rep on the specific phrasing of 'I prefer afternoon' or the 2 vs 3 PM choice as if it were his line — treat the actual afternoon/2PM preference as the customer's own statement, and note to the manager that the audio should be checked before using this segment to critique the rep's word choice.

quote: the appointment would be pretty quick, not too long at all. We just come by. It'd be about thirty minutes just to show it to you.
stewart_read: This is a clean, correct execution of the time-anchor protocol — the rep firmly quantifies the appointment length right after the customer signals a time-based hesitation, and it visibly works (the customer volunteers Monday immediately after).
coaching_implication: This is a positive, repeatable move — point to it as an example of anchoring time confidently per protocols.time_constraint when coaching other objection-timing moments.

quote: Just credit score needs to be about 670.
stewart_read: The call closes without a recap of the appointment, no one-hour block language, no no-driving/computer instruction, and no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake — the rep restates the credit threshold and the customer says goodbye.
coaching_implication: Button-up is skipped almost entirely. Coach the rep to run the full close checklist (recap day/time, set expectations for the visit, confirm verbally) even on short, seemingly-agreeable calls like this one.
